Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1225 PM CDT Tue Aug 04 2026

Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM MISSOURI
INTO ILLINOIS...NORTHEAST NEW MEXICO INTO THE TEXAS/OKLAHOMA
PANHANDLES...AND SOUTHEAST ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms appear possible from Missouri into central
Illinois, over portions of southeast Arizona, and from northeast New
Mexico into the Oklahoma/Texas Panhandles Wednesday afternoon and
evening.

...Missouri/Iowa/Illinois...
Broad troughing over the north-central CONUS into the Great Lakes
region will bring moderate to seasonably strong mid-level flow
across the Mid-Missouri/Mississippi Valleys. Large-scale lift will
not be overly strong, though embedded shortwave troughs may augment
lift locally. Along a surface trough from the lower Great Lakes
southwestward into the central Plains, dewpoints of mid/upper 60s to
low 70s F are expected. 1500-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE will be possible by
the afternoon. The strongest shear will likely remain on the cool
side of the surface boundary, but 30-35 kt of effective shear will
be sufficient for a few organized storms. Initial cells will be
capable of marginally severe hail. Clusters/linear segments will be
the predominant storm modes with an associated risk of damaging
winds.

...New Mexico into the Panhandles...
Moist upslope flow into the Raton Mesa will allow for storm
development by late afternoon. Modest northwesterly flow aloft
(around 35-40 kt of effective shear) will promote marginally
organized storms. Strong/severe winds will be the main hazard given
strong heating and steep low-level lapse rates.

...Arizona...
A moist airmass (50s to perhaps near 60 F dewpoints) will be in
place during the afternoon/evening. Westerly surface winds will
promote storm development within eastern portion of the Mogollon
Rim. Modest easterly winds aloft should be sufficient to move
activity off of the Rim into the lower deserts. Strong/severe wind
gusts will be possible especially where clustering of outflow
occurs.

..Wendt.. 08/04/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0229 PM CDT Tue Aug 04 2026

Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF THE
MID-ATLANTIC...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong storms may occur from the central Plains into the
Northeast on Thursday with locally strong wind gusts.

...Northeast...
A very moist airmass (dewpoints in the low/mid 70s F) are expected
across much of the East along the western periphery of the Atlantic
surface high. Flow aloft will be somewhat enhanced near the Great
Lakes trough, primarily for the northern Mid-Atlantic into parts of
New England. Given the rich moisture, surface heating will not have
to be overly robust to promote around or above 2000 J/kg MLCAPE
despite weak mid-level lapse rates. Where steeper low-level lapse
rates and/or clustering can occur, isolated damaging winds will be
possible.

...Central/Northern Plains...
Predictability continues to be low within these regions. In southern
Kansas, the cold font, perhaps augmented by early day
precipitation/clouds, will be one area of potential storm
development during the afternoon. Temperatures to the south of the
stalled boundary will be quite hot and may provide enough lift for
initiation. Enough mid-level flow will be present to promote storm
organization, should any form. Uncertainty in development remains
too high for a categorical risk area.

A secondary surface front is expected to develop from northern
Nebraska into the eastern Dakotas and northern Minnesota. The ECMWF
is much more aggressive with moisture return ahead of the boundary
than the NAM. Furthermore, mid-level heights will likely be slowly
rising through the period. A stronger storm or two would be
possible, but development is still uncertain. Elevated storms are
probable in northern Minnesota as the low-level jet increases, but
buoyancy is expected to remain weak.

..Wendt.. 08/04/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0400 AM CDT Tue Aug 04 2026

Valid 071200Z - 121200Z

...DISCUSSION...
An upper high will remain over the southwestern states through much
of the period, with a deep upper low gradually shifting eastward
across Ontario Canada. In between, a zone of moderate northwest flow
aloft will exist from the northern Plains/Upper MS Valley across the
Great Lakes. At the surface, low pressure will exist over the
central High Plains, with an east-west boundary roughly along I-80
from Nebraska eastward.

Stronger cyclonic flow aloft will move out of the northern Plains on
Fri/D4 and increase across the Great Lakes and into the Northeast
from Sat/D5 through the end of the period, with midlevel winds
around 30-40 kt possibly overspreading the surface front. A large
area of upper 60s to lower 70s F dewpoints will remain along and
south of the boundary, which may shift north/south as disturbances
rotate around the Canadian upper low. Predictability remains low for
denoting precise MCS corridors, but timing of the upper wave
amplifications will be monitored in subsequent forecast cycles, with
possible risk areas mainly for damaging wind potential.

..Jewell.. 08/04/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0740 PM CDT Tue Aug 04 2026

Valid 050100Z - 051200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
SOUTHERN ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts and hail will be possible this
evening in parts of southern Arizona, the southern Rockies, the
southern High Plains and the Upper Midwest.

...Southern Arizona...
The latest surface analysis shows a sufficiently moist airmass over
southern Arizona, where surface dewpoints are in the upper 50s to
around 60 F. This is contributing to moderate instability over parts
of southern Arizona, with the RAP suggesting that MLCAPE is in the
1000 to 2000 J/kg range. Thunderstorms have developed in the higher
terrain of southwest New Mexico. These storms will move
west-southwestward across southern Arizona this evening. In addition
to the instability, surface temperature-dewpoint spreads across this
airmass are large which is resulting in very steep low-level lapse
rates. This will contribute to a potential for severe wind gusts
this evening.

...Southern Rockies/Southern High Plains...
Scattered thunderstorms are ongoing in the southern Rockies early
this evening. These storms will move east-southeastward across
southeastern Colorado and northeastern New Mexico this evening,
where the RAP has SBCAPE around 1000 J/kg with moderate deep-layer
shear and steep low to mid-level lapse rates. The environment will
support an isolated potential for severe wind gusts and hail over
the next few hours.

...Upper Midwest...
An upper-level trough will move through the north-central U.S. this
evening. Ahead of the trough, a moist and unstable airmass will be
in place over the mid Missouri and mid to upper Mississippi Valleys.
An axis of low-level moisture is analyzed from northeast Kansas into
southeast Iowa, where surface dewpoints are in the 70s F. This is
contributing to moderate instability with the RAP showing MLCAPE in
the 2000 to 3500 J/kg range. Short-term model forecasts suggest that
scattered thunderstorms will develop near the instability axis
during the overnight period. The instability along with about 30
knots of 0-6 km shear will support an isolated wind-damage threat.

..Broyles.. 08/05/2026
